summary.short: Proposed federal bill, introduced 2 December 2025 and pending, that would bar developers and deployers from using covered algorithms in consequential actions in ways causing disparate impact or discrimination, require evaluations, impact assessments and disclosures, and allow FTC and state enforcement and private suits.
summary.long: H.R. 6356 (Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2025), introduced 2 December 2025 and pending, applies to developers and deployers of 'covered algorithms' used in 'consequential actions' such as employment, education, housing, credit, health care and criminal justice. Section 101 bars uses causing disparate impact or discrimination on protected characteristics. Section 102 requires pre-deployment evaluations, annual deployer impact assessments, developer reviews, reports to the Federal Trade Commission and ten-year retention. Title II adds mitigation, certification, deceptive-marketing and off-label use limits, developer-deployer contracts, human alternatives, appeal rights and anti-retaliation rules. Title III requires public disclosures, short-form notices and a reporting mechanism, and an FTC study. Violations are treated as unfair or deceptive practices under the FTC Act. State attorneys general and state data protection authorities may sue for civil penalties of $15,000 per violation or 4 percent of average gross annual revenue; individuals may sue for treble damages or $15,000 per violation. Pre-dispute arbitration agreements are unenforceable for disputes under the Act. No general effective date is stated; several rules are due within two years of enactment.

notes: Standalone bill introduced 2 Dec 2025 and referred to Energy and Commerce and Oversight and Government Reform. It amends and repeals no existing statute, so relations are cross-references only. Text quirks: a stray '@' precedes '(gg)' in Sec. 102(a)(2)(A)(ii); Sec. 2(5)(A)(iv) ends with 'or' before (B), and Sec. 101(b)(1)(C)(ii) ends with 'or' before (2). Sec. 102(b)(1)(A) refers to 'the developer's expected use' in a deployer assessment, apparently carried over from the developer text in Sec. 102(a)(1)(B)(i).
